Due to classification requirements, these offshore vessels need continuous maintenance, asset integrity management and regulatory compliance support to operate safely and efficiently. Put simply, lifecycle spending on keeping such assets running is a necessity, providing vendors, such as ASOM, with stable, sustainable and predictable revenue visibility.

Safety and reliability considerations mean that contractors such as ASOM, once appointed to undertake these projects, tend to “stick” around. “Once you get your foot in the door, you will typically get recurring work if you prove you are reliable and proficient with high safety standards,” says Yong. “The costs of switching are high for the asset operators as they need people whom they can trust to maintain safety and mission-worthiness, with downtime leading to revenue loss.”

From its recurrent income base, Beng Kuang, through ASOM, has earned its reputation as a trusted, safe and dependable partner. With a growing global presence, particularly in West Africa, its current clientele includes FPSO contractors/owners (such as SBM Offshore, MODEC, Yinson) as well as oil majors (such as Exxon Mobil).

“Under our Beng Kuang 2.0 roadmap, we have strengthened over the last few years and are focused on building a better-quality business model,” says Yong.

With the consolidation of ASOM into the group, Beng Kuang is positioned for its next phase of growth as it seeks to serve more offshore vessels while expanding the services provided to the 19 FPSOs and FSOs it currently supports.

According to data from the American Bureau of Shipping and Clarksons Research, there are more than 330 FPSO and FSO vessels operating worldwide, with new additions over the next few years bringing the total to above 400, hinting at the size of the market.

With major offshore work progressing and life-extension contracts secured, the business is building a stronger foundation for future earnings. Yong believes the opportunity lies not simply in winning more contracts, but also in developing long-term customer relationships that generate repeat business.

“We want customers to keep coming back to us because they trust our work. That gives us more repeat business, more stable earnings and better cash flow. Ultimately, we want to build a business that can grow steadily and reward our shareholders over the long term.”

In addition, Beng Kuang is not just limited to servicing FPSOs and FSOs, as its asset integrity solutions are applicable across other offshore assets, including floating liquefied natural gas (FLNG) vessels and floating, storage and regasification units (FSRU), which are projected to rise as energy security and demand drives gas extraction and production.

A foundation of Beng Kuang’s business is its corrosion protection solutions, which serve as the company’s “steady” cash base. With a track record of more than 30 years, the division works on a resident contractor model and sees recurring work.

The group’s International Offshore Equipments (IOE) specialises in the design, build and supply of marine and offshore deck equipment, and also provides after-sale services on supply of spare parts, servicing and upgrading recommendations and works.

Beng Kuang is also exploring the potential of shipbuilding and chartering. It has formed a joint venture (JV) with commercial ship owner and maritime management company Epsilon Navigation in April. Under the collaboration, the new JV seeks to execute a ‘build, charter, optimise, monetise and reinvest’ platform strategy for marine asset monetisation.

Since its turnaround to profitability in FY2024, Beng Kuang has rewarded shareholders via free warrants and resumption of annual dividends.

In September 2024, the company issued approximately 59.8 million of free warrants with each warrant allowing the holder to subscribe for one new ordinary share at 22 cents. As at Oct 12, Beng Kuang’s share price is 38 cents, representing an upside of around 73% to the exercise price.

“Building on our positive momentum, we’ve been unlocking shareholder value over the last few years,” says Yong, who reiterates that Beng Kuang’s transition to an asset-light, service-centric model has been deliberate.

“We are well-positioned with a proven track record of disciplined execution and reliability,” he adds. “Under our 2.0 roadmap, we have a clear strategic direction focused on building a quality, sustainable business. As we grow, we remain committed to sharing the benefits of that growth with our shareholders and rewarding them for their continued support.”
